resources.string: Home and navigation
Find a safe starting point
Start here
Home is the launch point for tools, recent work, resources, and settings. Use search, pinned items, menus, or a resource card to open the area you need.
Check the result
Check the destination title, status text, and Back path. Keep the current screen open while you decide what to do next.
Fix a problem
If a sheet or destination is confusing, read its status, close it, and return to the owning hub with Back before trying again.
AI tools hub
Choose a tool safely
Start here
Tools groups conversation, creation, voice, documents, Organizer, and infrastructure. Search by name or keyword, then open a category or tool card to see its options.
Check the result
Check the selected tool\'s model, server, storage, and microphone status before opening a task.
Fix a problem
If a tool reports a missing requirement, open the linked manager or Settings page, read the message, then return with Back.
Start here
Check the result
Fix a problem
Model management and bundles
Model manager quickstart
Model Hub separates installed files, active downloads, discovery, sources, and family managers. Open a family tab and read a model card’s size, source, and compatibility before choosing an action.
Check whether the tab shows installed, downloading, discover, or empty content; model family, size, source, compatibility, and storage appear on the card.
If a card is unavailable, close its details, return to Model Hub, and follow the manager or storage message before trying again.
Choose an LLM file and companion

Open an LLM row and check its GGUF format, quantization, and file role. For a vision model, keep its matching projector visible beside it; optional draft models appear separately. Read the file, vision, projector, and storage details before queueing it.
Check the filename, GGUF format, quantization, vision capability, projector relationship, size, and source. If a companion is missing, the row names the matching file so you can add it.
If a file will not work, keep the row selected and follow its format or companion message. Return to the LLM manager or saved source to correct that item, then try again.
Inspect Stable Diffusion components

Open the Stable Diffusion manager and choose a component row. Check whether it is a checkpoint, diffusion model, VAE, CLIP or T5 encoder, ControlNet, or LoRA, then read its family, variant, and compatible profile.
Check the component role, backend metadata, supported image or video profiles, and any companion warning before selecting it in a workflow.
If a profile rejects the component, keep it and follow the role or compatibility message. Return to the SD manager and replace only the missing or mismatched component.
Review an ONNX directory bundle
Open an ONNX bundle row and review its graph, external weights, tokenizer, and pipeline metadata. Use the asset and storage details to confirm that the directory is complete.
Check the directory layout, pipeline family, input and output capability, and source. An incomplete bundle names the graph, weights, or metadata that is missing.
Return to the ONNX manager or source browser and add the named item; leave the incomplete bundle unchanged until validation passes.
Select a LiteRT backend safely
Open LiteRT model details and choose CPU, GPU, MTP, or another available accelerator. Compare the model’s memory and context needs before loading it.
Check the model path, input shape or role, selected backend, availability, and memory warning. An unavailable accelerator stays marked unavailable instead of being chosen silently.
If memory or backend validation fails, follow the message and choose a compatible backend. Keep the model selection and try loading again when the warning clears.
Pair Whisper transcription with VAD
Open Whisper model settings and check the speech-to-text file, optional VAD file, language, thread count, threshold, and duration controls. VAD gates speech only when its model is available.
Check the Whisper and VAD paths, enabled state, threshold and duration range, and thread count. A missing VAD path explains a disabled gate.
If VAD or a setting is unavailable, follow the named asset or range message and return to model management before changing it.
Inspect a custom model URL

Open the model family manager and use Custom download. Paste a direct HTTPS file link, then tap Download. Optional details lets you add a label or choose a component type; Automatic detection is the default. The app saves the source and queues download and inspection.
Follow the pending item in the download or pending tab. Its filename, family, source URL, validation state, and any authentication or network message show whether the file can be promoted.
If validation fails, read the exact message, clear or correct the URL, label, or role, and submit it again. A saved source remains available in Sources for editing or verification.
Review saved model links
In Sources, open a saved link and use Verify to check it before staging an artifact. Use Browse for a Hugging Face repository, or Edit to change its family, URL, or label and press Save.
Check the host, family, source type, verification state, authentication requirement, and the detail returned by Verify or Browse.
Dismiss the error and keep the last valid link. Correct only the named prerequisite, then run Verify or Browse again from the source card.
Recover an Unknown model state

Open the Unknown tab and select a staged artifact to read its filename, detected family, requested role, and validation details. Choose Inspect first; use Promote only after you confirm the family and role.
The detail shows the staging path, detected type, requested role, and the recognition or validation reason. Promote lets you assign the confirmed family, display name, role, and metadata.
If recognition is incomplete, keep the staged artifact, close its detail, and correct the family or role in Promote. Retry the artifact only after the displayed requirement is clear.
Browse a Hugging Face folder

In Sources, open a Hugging Face link and tap Browse. Enter a repository folder, move through pages, and select the compatible file; the browser copies its direct file URL, filename, and family context into Custom download. Keep companion files from the same folder together when the model needs them.
Check the repository and folder path, revision, file or directory type, page count, size, and the selected file URL. Authentication, invalid paths, and network failures appear in the browser message.

Go up or close the folder dialog, correct only the repository, path, token, or network issue named by the message, and open Browse again. Select a file only after its metadata matches the model family.
Inspect model bundles

Open Bundles and tap Create bundle. Give it a name and family, then add the installed files or saved sources that belong together and assign each item its role. Save the definition when every required item is present.
Open the bundle card to verify its name, family, members, roles, source links, and readiness. Missing sources, unverified links, and incomplete split or directory groups are listed on the card.
Edit the bundle and repair the named source, path, role, or companion group. Verify its links, save the definition, then use Download missing when the card reports Ready.
Review local model import

Open the model manager’s Import or installed-assets section and choose a local file or directory when you are ready. Review the detected family, type, capabilities, and destination before confirming the import.
Check the filename, detected type, vision or embedding capability, overwrite rule, and import progress. A validation message explains a file that cannot be accepted.
Cancel the picker or import, keep installed files unchanged, and follow the validation or rename message before choosing another local file.
Inspect model sharing
Open Model Share and read the local address, QR or URL, available model count, and active transfers. Use Share or Copy when you want to expose the current library to another device.
Check the local interface, model count, active transfer count, QR or URL details, and the current transfer state.
Stop an active share or transfer from this screen, then return to the model manager. The installed set remains available after the status settles.
Image workspaces
Inspect image creation modes
Open Image Generation and switch between Create and Gallery. In Create, choose a mode, model, prompt, and settings; Gallery shows progress and saved results.
Check the mode, model readiness, draft prompt, options, gallery, progress, and any failure message.
If a render cannot start, keep the draft and source, follow the model or backend message to its manager, then return and try again.
Review inpaint and image options
Open Inpaint or image-to-image, choose a source when ready, then check the mask, denoise or strength, dimensions, seed, and prompt options.
Check the source and mask requirements, option ranges, preview, and which actions remain disabled until the input is valid.
Clear only an invalid mask or input, keep the draft, and follow the range or format message before trying again.
Inspect ONNX image generation
Open ONNX Image Generation, choose the text or image input mode, and review the model and gallery controls. The local preview and result path appear after a run completes.
Check model readiness, input mode, progress, local preview, and the path used for a saved result.
If the model is unavailable, keep the source, open ONNX model management from the status message, and return when it reports Ready.
Inspect ONNX background removal
Open Background Removal, choose an image, and review the before and after preview, model status, output format, Save, and Share controls.
Check the input requirement, model readiness, alpha preview, output format, and any edge or processing message.
Keep the original image, follow the edge or model diagnostic, and choose a valid input or return to model management before trying again.
Video tools
Inspect video creation and gallery
Tap Create to set up a video. Start with the prompt and model sections, then review the selected workflow.
Choose a profile such as Wan or LingBot and check its components, workflow, and input requirements before starting a run.
Tap Gallery to review saved video cards. Return to Create if a component or workflow message needs correction.
Compare expanded video families
Tap Create before comparing the available video family profiles.
Choose Wan, HunyuanVideo, LingBot, LTX, MiniMax, SVD, or AnimateDiff and review each profile’s components, inputs, audio, and hires options.
Tap Gallery to leave the profile editor; return to Create and follow the message if a selected family needs different components.
Review LingBot video inputs
Tap Create to open the video setup; the profile selector is where LingBot is applied.
Choose LingBot, review its caption format and frame limits, and add an image only when switching to image-to-video.
Tap Gallery to leave setup. Return to Create if a component or workflow message needs correction.
Review video LoRA controls
Tap Create before opening Advanced video options.
Open Advanced, expand LoRA, choose an adapter, set its weight, and check profile compatibility and order.
Tap Gallery when you finish reviewing the draft; return to Create to remove an invalid adapter or restore its last valid weight.
Review video upscaling
Open Video Upscaler, choose a source video and model, then set scale, quality, output, and storage options. Use the preview and Stop controls as needed.
Check source validation, model readiness, scale, output path, audio behavior, and frame progress.
Keep the original video, follow the file, model, or storage diagnostic, and repair only that prerequisite before trying again.
Review video interpolation
Open Video Interpolation, choose the source and RIFE model, set source and target FPS, and review scene-cut, audio, and output options.
Check source and target FPS, model readiness, scene-cut behavior, audio restoration, and frame progress.
Keep the original video, follow the FPS or model message, and correct only the named option before trying again.
Review subtitle burn
Open Subtitle Burn, choose a video and subtitle file, then set font, placement, codec, and output options. Use Preview before starting the encode.
Check subtitle parsing, style and placement, codec, output path, and encoding progress.
Keep the original video and subtitle file, follow the subtitle or codec log, and correct only the named input or style before trying again.
Inspect video summary stages
Open Video Summary, choose a video, Whisper model, and summary backend, then follow extraction, transcript, summary, and optional Organizer save stages.
Check the current phase, transcript availability, summary status, and the destination selected for an optional saved note.
Keep the source video, follow the failed phase, and repair the named Whisper or backend prerequisite before trying again.
Voice and speech
Inspect ONNX text to speech

ONNX TTS turns text into local audio and keeps model, speaker, rate, playback, and gallery state together. A compatible TTS model is readiness only for generation. Use the model, language, text, speaker, rate, play, stop, and gallery icons. Read the empty form.
Check that model readiness, language, speaker, draft text, audio result, and playback state are explicit.
Preserve text, open ONNX model management from the status message, and return after the model is ready.
Inspect live translation turns

Live Translator keeps source and target languages, microphone permission, turn state, and translated speech visible. When you capture a turn, choose permission and speech models. Use the language pair, swap, microphone, speaker, stop, and turn history icons. Inspect the pair and review the settings.
Check that ready, listening, translated, stopped, permission, and connection states are easy to scan.
Stop the turn, read the permission or connection message, and reselect the language pair before speaking later.
Inspect Whisper transcription

Audio Transcription separates file or microphone input, Whisper model, language, timestamps, transcript, and retry. When you transcribe, choose a readable audio file and model. Use the file, microphone, model, language, timestamps, record, stop, and copy icons. Read the empty state.
Check that input, model readiness, transcript editing, copy, and decoding error states are explicit.
Preserve the source audio, read the decoder error, and repair the model or input before retrying.
Documents and workflows
Inspect PDF toolbox and summary

PDF Toolbox separates page preview, extraction, OCR, summary, translation, and export actions. When you use it, choose a readable PDF and model. Use the file, pages, OCR, search, summary, copy, share, and cancel icons. Switch tabs and review the current state.
Check that page count, extraction, OCR or summary readiness, easy to scan text, and output actions are explicit.
Keep the original PDF, read the page or backend diagnostic, and retry only the narrower operation after fixing its prerequisite.
Inspect workflows and dataset processing

Workflows and Dataset projects show steps, sources, chunks, processing, review, queue, and settings before a run. Start from an existing definition or empty project. Use the nodes, source, chunks, review, queue, settings, run, and stop icons. Open a tab and read the current state.
Check that validation, source state, chunk count, queue, review, and run status are clear and easy to read.
Stop a queued run, return to the owning project, and read the exact failed step before retrying.
Review video summary as a document result
Video Summary keeps extraction, Whisper transcription, AI summary, and the optional Organizer note stages visible. Open the stage list to see where a result stopped and what to do next.
Check the extraction phase, transcript, summary, note destination, and error stage.
Return to the failed stage, follow its model, backend, or storage message, and keep the source and text intact while you try again.
Review Dataset project tabs

Dataset projects keep Sources, Chunks, Process, Review, Queue, and Settings separate so readiness is visible. Start from an existing or empty project. Use the project, sources, chunks, process, review, queue, settings, and back icons. Switch tabs and read the project tabs.
Check that project metadata, source status, chunk count, processing state, review state, and queue are explicit.
Return to the project list, preserve existing sources, and read the blocked prerequisite before retrying.
Conversations and native servers
Inspect Chat server selection

Chat keeps server choice, composer, attachments, generation status, and stop recovery together. When you respond, choose a running server. Use the server chip, composer, send, stop, and attachment icons. Open server selection and choose an endpoint when ready.
Check that no server, one server, selected endpoint, generating, stopped, and error states are explicit. Read endpoint and easy to scan message status before sending.
Stop generation, choose another endpoint, or open server management after reading the error.
Review native llama server cards
Open a native llama server card to review its saved command, model path, port, process state, logs, and edit controls. Start or stop the process from the same card when you are ready.
Check the stopped, loading, running, or error state together with the command and log details.
Leave a failing card stopped, correct only the named path or port, and read the diagnostic before starting it again.
Review chat history and folders
Open a chat session row or folder to review recent conversations, search, rename, archive, and the message preview. The session card keeps its title, server, folder, and updated time together.
Check the title, server identity, updated time, folder, and message preview on the session card.
Return to the history list and keep the session saved. If its server is unavailable, follow that status before opening it again.
Review scheduled native tasks
Scheduler separates task definitions, schedule status, run logs, and stop or disable controls. Start from existing or empty task lists.
Check that task name, trigger, enabled state, next run, last status, and easy to scan logs are explicit.
Disable a failed task, read its log, and return to the task list before editing a schedule.
Compare server selection paths
The server chooser connects Chat, native cards, and saved local endpoints while showing which process owns a port.
Check available, stopped, loading, and unavailable server cards show endpoint, owner, and action boundaries.
Close the chooser, return to the owning hub, and read the endpoint diagnostic before selecting another server.
AI Agent workspace
Inspect the Agent workspace

Agent workspace separates project context, plan, approvals, tool output, stop, and Continue recovery. When you run a task, choose a project and backend. Use the project, robot, plan, approval, stop, and Continue icons. Read the current workspace state.
Check that idle, planning, approval, running, completed, and interrupted states are explicit.
Choose Continue only after the interruption reason is clear, or Stop to leave the task recoverable.
Review Agent projects and files

Agent projects keep root folder, file tree, recent changes, and project settings visible before a run. Start from an existing or empty project. Use the project picker, folder, file, changed, refresh, and back icons. Inspect project metadata and read the current details.
Check that root path, file count, changed-file status, and unavailable-folder explanation are easy to scan.
Return to project selection, preserve files, and repair only the displayed permission or path requirement before reopening.
Review Agent plans and configuration

Plans expose ordered steps, tool intent, model or backend configuration, and approval boundaries before execution. Start from an existing plan or empty state. Use the plan, step, edit, backend, model, approval, and collapse icons. Read the plan and read the current settings.
Check that step order, prerequisite, pending approval, and selected runtime are explicit.
Close the plan, keep the last saved configuration, and return to the blocked prerequisite before continuing.
Review Agent approvals and tool boundaries

Approval queue shows the tool, scope, proposed effect, and Continue or Stop decision before it runs. An empty queue is a valid safe state. Use the approval, scope, allow, deny, stop, and Continue controls. Read a pending request or empty state.
Check that requested tool, target path, reason, decision state, and interrupted recovery path are easy to scan.
Deny or stop an unclear request, keep the task paused, and use Continue only after scope is understood.
Review Agent invocation recovery

Review the saved phase, tool metadata, and sanitized error. In Agent, use Continue when interrupted work offers it. Open an invocation from the workspace to inspect its history; if none exists, use Preview or Skip.
Check the phase, status, timing, tool name, sanitized error, and next safe action.
Keep the diagnostic and return to Agent for the available Continue or Stop controls. A terminal invocation remains readable without restarting work.
Organizer
Review Organizer notes
Notes tab separates saved notes, search, filters, detail, and edit actions. Start from existing or empty notes.
Check that title, updated time, preview, tags, and read-only detail are easy to scan.
Dismiss the editor, preserve the last saved note, and read the validation message before editing later.
Review Organizer calendar

Calendar tab keeps date navigation, event rows, AI schedule status, and detail dialogs separate. Start from an empty calendar. Use the date, calendar, event, schedule, filter, and detail icons. Change the visible day and review the current state.
Check that selected date, event time, reminder status, and empty-day recovery are explicit.
Close event details, return to the selected date, and preserve saved events before retrying a failed reminder.
Review Organizer alarms

Alarms tab exposes enabled state, time, repeat rule, label, and dismissal without triggering a reminder. Start from existing or empty alarms. Use the alarm, time, repeat, enabled, dismiss, and detail icons. Inspect an alarm row.
Check that next trigger, repeat rule, enabled state, and validation or permission status are visible.
Disable an invalid alarm, close details, and return to the alarm list after reading the permission message.
Review Organizer editors and dialogs

Note, event, alarm, fullscreen, and image dialogs keep drafts, validation, cancel, and save boundaries explicit. Start from opening a dialog with an empty draft. Use the title, body, date, image, cancel, save, and close icons. Open and dismiss a detail dialog.
Check that draft ownership, required fields, validation, and cancel behavior are readable.
Cancel the draft, preserve saved data, and reopen the owning tab after reading the validation error.
Library and resources
Review the local Library
Library groups model, offline, and reference resources with source, readiness, size, and open actions. Start from an empty or installed library.
Check that resource type, availability, size, source, and open or share action are explicit.
Return to the library list, preserve installed resources, and read the unavailable reason before trying a resource later.
Knowledge Base
Review Knowledge Base sources

Knowledge Base lists sources, index status, chunk count, search, and source actions. Existing or empty sources are safe to inspect. Use the source, index, chunks, search, delete, and detail icons. Open a source row and read the source status.
Check that source path, status, chunk count, last update, and blocked prerequisite are easy to scan.
Preserve the source, close details, and repair only the displayed path, model, or storage issue before indexing later.
Review Knowledge Base search

Knowledge search separates query, result score, source citation, chunk preview, and empty-state recovery. Start from an empty index. Use the search, filter, score, source, chunk, and clear icons. Read the search form and keep the draft open.
Check that query state, no-result reason, result rank, citation, and easy to scan chunk text are explicit.
Clear the query, return to sources, and read the index or embedding prerequisite before searching later.
Review Knowledge chunk reading

Open an indexed source and choose a chunk to read its source, position, and bounded text. Use Previous, Next, Copy, and Back. This guide stays in an open reader; without indexed content, use Preview or Skip.
Check that source, position, text preview, and missing-chunk status are easy to scan.
Return to the source list, preserve indexed data, and use the source status before reopening a missing chunk.
Offline reading
Manage offline Kiwix content

Kiwix separates installed ZIMs, catalog metadata, downloading, sharing, and settings. Start from installed or empty catalog. Use the Installed, Catalog, Downloading, Share, Settings, size, and language icons. Switch tabs and read the current status.
Check that language, size, source, installed state, progress, and storage status are explicit.
Cancel only a pending transfer, return to Installed, and read the catalog or storage error before retrying.
Review offline reading
Open an installed ZIM and select an article in the Kiwix reader. The reader keeps the article title, loading state, source, sharing action, and return path together.
Check the reader title, article loading state, offline availability, and the visible return path.
Return to the ZIM list and follow the viewer message if an article cannot be opened.
Servers and LAN access
Review local server hub
Server Hub groups local AI server cards, endpoint health, ports, start or stop, edit, and logs. Start from cards. Use the server, endpoint, port, play, stop, edit, and logs icons. Open a card status.
Check that endpoint, process owner, running or stopped state, port, and easy to scan logs are explicit.
Keep a failing process stopped, correct only the named endpoint or port, and reread the card status before starting later.
Review the LAN file server

File Server exposes shared folder, local URL, QR, permissions, and active share status while showing the folder boundary. Start from the screen. Use the folder, URL, QR, permission, start, stop, and copy icons. Read the current folder and status.
Check that folder path, local address, permission, running state, and easy to scan share instructions are visible.
Stop an active share, choose a valid folder or free port later, and reread the status before sharing.
Review Ollama servers and models
Open Ollama and switch between Servers and Models. Review an endpoint card, model inventory, pull status, health, and logs; use Add or Edit when you are ready to change a card.
Check endpoint health, model state, pull progress, and the reason shown for an unavailable server or model.
Cancel a pending pull, keep the server card, and follow its endpoint or model message before trying again.
Distributed LLM runtime
Choose a distributed role
Distributed Hub separates master, worker, and network paths before a service changes ports or memory. Use the Master, Worker, Network, endpoint, and status cards. Read role descriptions.
Check that role purpose, endpoint, running state, and navigation path are explicit.
Return to the hub, keep services stopped, and open the role card matching the displayed prerequisite.
Configure the distributed master

Master setup selects a local model, assigns workers, reviews layer placement, and exposes start or stop state before serving inference. A model and worker are optional for inspection. Use the model, workers, placement, command preview, start, stop, and network status. Read the current model and worker state.
Check that model identity, worker assignments, layer allocation, endpoint state, and launch readiness are explicit.
Keep the master stopped, correct only the missing model, worker, or placement prerequisite, and reread the readiness message before starting.
Review distributed worker setup

Worker setup keeps identity, master endpoint, advertised capacity, memory budget, and running status visible. Start from a worker. Use the worker name, master URL, RAM, budget, save, start, stop, and status icons. Read the effective budget and review the current state.
Check that identity, endpoint, real or estimated metrics, freshness, applied budget, and stopped or running state are explicit.
Stop the worker, correct the endpoint or budget, and apply only a changed contribution before starting later.
Read distributed topology and diagnostics

Open Network view to see the master and worker nodes connected by graphical edges. Each node shows its name, endpoint, status, identifier, real or estimated metrics, freshness, and a short log preview.
Check each edge, metric source, freshness, endpoint, identifier, service status, and visible log preview.
Refresh once, read the stale or unavailable detail, and open the owning service card to correct the problem.
Distributed media runtime
Choose distributed media roles

Distributed media Hub separates master, worker, network, run configuration, and gallery before a render. Use the master, worker, network, config, gallery, status, and back icons. Read role descriptions.
Check that role, endpoint, queue ownership, output destination, and unavailable state are clear.
Return to the media hub, preserve existing output, and read the role prerequisite before opening a service later.
Review distributed media workers

Media topology shows worker graph, assignment, queue state, connection status, and real or estimated metrics before a run starts. Empty workers are valid. Use the graph, worker, assignment, queue, status, refresh, endpoint, and logs icons. Inspect the graph.
Check that worker assignment, queue freshness, endpoint, identifier, metric source, and easy to scan error are visible.
Refresh once, preserve run configuration, and return to the worker or master card named by the error.
Review distributed media configuration and gallery

Run Configuration and Gallery keep workflow, queue, output metadata, and completed media separate. Start from an empty queue or existing result. Use the config, queue, output, gallery, metadata, cancel, and back icons. Switch to Gallery and keep the draft open.
Check that configuration readiness, queue state, output path, result metadata, and cancellation state are easy to scan.
Cancel only a queued run, return to configuration, and preserve completed output before retrying.
Benchmark and history
Review benchmark setup and results

Benchmark separates device readiness, thread settings, duration, progress, score, and diagnostics. Start from the setup screen. Use the device, threads, duration, run, stop, score, and status icons. Read current settings.
Check that device, thread count, duration, score source, unavailable reason, and easy to scan progress are explicit.
Stop an active run, preserve history, and repair only the named device or configuration prerequisite before retrying.
Review benchmark history

Benchmark History keeps prior scores, model or device identity, duration, comparison, and deletion boundaries readable. Empty history is valid. Use the history rows, device, score, compare, export, delete, and back icons. Open a prior result or empty state.
Check that run date, device, model, score, duration, and unavailable metadata are easy to scan.
Close details, preserve records, and return to Benchmark after reading the missing artifact reason.
Quadtrix training workspace
Review Quadtrix training configuration

Quadtrix keeps project, dataset, epochs, checkpoint, backend, output, and validation visible before training. Start from an existing or empty project. Use the project, dataset, epochs, checkpoint, output, run, and stop icons. Read configuration.
Check that project path, dataset readiness, training parameters, output destination, and validation state are explicit.
Keep artifacts unchanged, return to the blocked field, and repair only the named project or dataset prerequisite.
Review Quadtrix progress and WebUI

Open Quadtrix progress to follow the current phase, metrics, logs, artifact path, Stop action, and WebUI handoff. Use the status card to distinguish queued, running, completed, failed, and unavailable states.
Check the phase, metrics, log preview, artifact path, stop state, and WebUI availability.
Stop an active run if needed, keep its logs and artifacts, and follow the failed phase before reopening WebUI.
Termux and file tools
Review Termux shell tools
Open a Termux tool to review its host, command preview, permission, connection state, output, and Stop action. Run a command only after the preview and host are correct.
Check the tool name, host, permission, command preview, exit state, and readable output.
Cancel a command, return to the tool list, and follow the permission or connection message before trying again.
Review Termux WebView tools
Termux WebView keeps tool identity, URL, title, loading status, and return path separate from the shell. Start from an existing tool or empty state.
Check that uRL, tool title, loading, blocked, and unavailable states are easy to scan.
Close WebView, return to Termux tools, and read the URL or permission error before trying another tool.
Review Termux file manager

Termux File Manager exposes path, folder, permissions, selection, copy, and return actions before running commands. Start from an empty or existing folder. Use the path, folder, file, permission, copy, open, and back icons. Read the current folder.
Check that path, item type, permission, selected state, and unavailable-folder message are explicit.
Return to the parent folder, preserve selection, and read the permission or path error before retrying.
Settings and help
Review appearance settings

General settings groups theme, density, font scaling, navigation, and visual behavior. Start by checking current values. Use the theme, color, density, font, navigation, reset, and back icons. Inspect the current appearance values.
Check that active theme, display scale, font scale, and persistence or reset meaning are clear.
Keep the last valid value, dismiss validation, and return to General settings before changing another option.
Review language and locale settings

Language settings explain localized copy, locale selection, and restart or persistence behavior. Reading the current locale is safe. Use the language, locale, apply, restart, reset, and back icons. Read the selected language and read the current settings.
Check that current locale, available languages, restart requirement, and fallback behavior are explicit.
Keep the current locale, dismiss the notice, and return to General settings if a language is unavailable.
Review settings backup and restore

Backup controls explain export, import, file destination, compatibility, and confirmation before settings change. Start from the backup section. Use the backup, restore, file, export, import, overwrite, and cancel icons. Read the backup policy.
Check that included settings, destination, version compatibility, overwrite warning, and validation are explicit.
Cancel the picker, preserve current settings, and read the import or version error before restoring later.
Review prompt templates

Prompt settings separate selected template, PDF summary prompts, reset, edit, and save boundaries. Existing or default prompts can be read without editing. Use the template, prompt, edit, reset, save, and cancel icons. Inspect a prompt card.
Check that selected template, scope, fallback, and reset behavior are easy to scan.
Cancel the editor, preserve the last saved prompt, and restore defaults only after reading the scope message.
Review logs and diagnostics

Open Diagnostics to review event type, phase, status, timing, counts, connection state, and sanitized errors. Continue is available when an interrupted operation has a safe next step; Clear removes the visible records.
Check the event metadata, phase, status, timing, sanitized error class, and offered recovery action.
Keep the records while investigating a failure, use Continue only when it is offered, and return to the owning surface after reading the diagnostic.
Review About and support links

About combines version, build provenance, libraries, developer information, support links, and compatibility notes. Use the version, build, libraries, GitHub, support, Ko-fi, PayPal, and back icons. Read the version card.
Check that app version, native build status, licenses, support destinations, and unavailable link state are easy to scan.
Close the external link or dialog, return to About, and preserve the app state if a support link is unavailable.

FastSD gallery
Read the Tama room
Open the Tama room to see pet status, room actions, the map, menu, and companion art. Start from the setup prompt or current pet status, then open a room card or map.
Check the pet name, needs, time, current room or map, and available actions. The first screen links to care, inventory, gallery, and settings.
If a menu or dialog is unclear, close it, return to the room with Back, and follow the setup message before trying an action.
Inspect Tama care actions
Open Care and read the feeding, rest, hygiene, health, study, work, and exercise labels with their prerequisites. Start with the status values and open an action dialog when you are ready.
Check energy, hunger, health, hygiene, education, and exercise requirements. A disabled action explains which need is missing.
Close the action dialog, keep the current status, and follow its displayed prerequisite before trying again. If it is unavailable, wait or correct that prerequisite instead of tapping repeatedly.
Open Tama chat and gallery
Open Tama Chat or Gallery to keep pet conversation settings separate from saved artwork. Review the chat and gallery headers, then choose a backend or gallery item when ready.
Check backend readiness, model or voice options, saved artwork, and gallery state. Empty states explain which option to set up next.
Return to Tama, close an unavailable backend message or gallery preview, and follow its status before trying again.
Inspect the Tama farm
Open Farm to review plots, crops, helpers, storage, and farm actions on one scrollable surface. Select a plot or section to read its current state.
Check plot state, crop timing, inventory, and helper status. Empty and locked states explain what is unavailable, and the farm remains readable on a phone.
Close a detail dialog, return to the farm grid, and follow the named resource or unlock requirement before trying an action.
Inspect Tama animal care
Open Barn or Coop to review animal counts, stored output, hunger, feed availability, and the return controls. Switch feed inspection or read the header before choosing an animal action.
Check the current Barn or Coop title, storage, animal slots, hunger state, and feed controls. Empty slots and unavailable actions explain their state.
Turn off feed inspection and use Back to return to Farm. Follow the named feed or unlock requirement before feeding, collecting output, or buying livestock.
Browse the Tama store
Open the Store and choose a category to review item cards, prices, stock, and purchase effects. Open an item card to see its confirmation path.
Check the item name, price, availability, effect, and confirmation path. Empty stock or insufficient funds remains visible on the card.
Close the item detail, return to Farm or the room, and follow the availability message before trying the purchase again.
Browse Tama arcade games
Open Arcade and choose a game card to read its rules and entry requirements. Open the details before starting a round.
Check the game title, rules, cost or energy requirement, and return path. A locked game explains what is missing.
Leave the game selector with Back, close the rules dialog, and return to the room if the game is unavailable.
Inspect dungeon selection
Open Dungeon selection and choose an available or locked entry to compare adventure paths, difficulty, and entry status.
Check dungeon name, status, requirements, and start or return controls. The list remains scrollable when more paths are present.
Return to the Tama room, close settings, and follow the displayed unlock requirement before entering a path.
Read an adventure scene
Open an Adventure scene to read its narrative, choices, status, and return path. Review the scene before choosing how to continue.
Check scene text, available choices, health or energy status, and progression state. Locked or completed scenes explain their state.
Use the scene Back path or close its settings, keep the current progress, and read the displayed state before trying again.
Inspect the adventure gate
Open the Adventure gate to review entry, opponent, party status, and battle readiness before a Tama battle. Read the gate status and readiness checks first.
Check opponent details, readiness checks, rewards, and cancel or return controls. Missing energy or party requirements are shown clearly.
Cancel the gate dialog or return to the room, then follow only the named prerequisite before opening it again.
Browse the night arena
Open Night Arena to review its sleep-time entry state, opponents, and battle controls. Read the status before starting a match.
Check arena availability, opponent state, energy or time requirement, and exit path. An unavailable state explains why entry is disabled.
Leave the arena with Back, keep the displayed state, and return when its prerequisite is met.
Inspect the FastSD gallery
Open FastSD Gallery to browse generated image files in the configured remote results folder. Review connection, preview, selection, share, and delete controls.
Check the connection state, image grid, file metadata, loading progress, and empty or failure message. Open a preview from the gallery when you need to inspect a file.
Return after SSH connects, close a preview, or clear the selection after reading the error.
